program.school: School of Construction and the Environment

offerings.status: Refer to official BCIT program page

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course develops a range of architectural graphics skills and strategies for various design communications. The course is structured around a series of manual drawing exercises, exploring two- and three-dimensional representation techniques and digital post-processing to produce effective architectural graphics for different purposes. The course emphasizes graphic communication as a means of exploring architectural potential, articulating design intent, and documenting meaningful project information. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this studio is to introduce architectural design as an iterative process of inquiry and experimentation. A series of exercises will provide a structured approach to architectural process and methods (including physical models, concept diagrams, precedent studies and presentation drawings). Students will build on skills acquired in previous architectural and building technology diploma courses to implement first principles of architectural design on small site-specific projects. Detailed context analysis will be conducted to inform meaningful and sustainable architectural solutions. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this course is to explore the global history of architecture with a post-colonial lens. The course follows a rough chronological arc from the emergence of First Civilizations to the twentieth century. Evolutions of building typologies, materials, systems and methods are examined within the context of the prevailing social, political and economic forces of particular times in history, in cultures around the world. In addition to course lectures and discussions, students will research areas of interest and participate in knowledge sharing with the class. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Through a series of lectures and work assignments, this course will introduce students to broad principles in building science and performance and will provide learning opportunities for basic application of these principles. Students will learn these principles through the lens of the four elements in building science studies: i) exterior climate and region, ii) wall and separator, iii) user and occupant, iv) energy and technology.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this course is to present learning resources and metrics to identify, measure and value sustainability in architecture and building construction. Students will develop a thorough understanding of environmentally responsible design, considering both the technical performance of individual buildings and the social context within which sustainability is now being framed. Through a series of lectures and case studies, students will learn to read and apply green building rating systems and assess the impacts of sustainable design strategies. Using a data-driven approach, students will be able to advocate effectively for sustainable design and environmental responsibilities. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: 50% in BCIT ENGL 1177 or equivalent, or 6 credits BCIT Communication at 1100-level or above, or 3 credits of a university/college first-year social science or humanities course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This is a course in advanced composition and rhetoric, in which students will develop skills in complex critical analysis and interpretation by analyzing and evaluating materials from a variety of discourses or genres, including visual, online, and print; developing and writing essays, including critiques and research papers; applying and discussing principles of rhetoric and critical theory; examining and using methods of interpretation and analysis from the humanities and social sciences; evaluating the credibility of primary and secondary sources, including as it applies to media literacy, and for the purposes of academic research; situating discourses within their historical context and relevant to rhetorical theories of different periods (for example, Aristotle in the ancient world and Bakhtin in the twentieth century). The course format will include lecture, discussion, and both individual and group activities. Prerequisite(s): 50% in BCIT ENGL 1177 or equivalent, or 6 credits BCIT Communication at 1100-level or above, or 3 credits of a university/college first-year social science or humanities course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 5005 and ARSC 5000
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this studio is to develop an architectural approach to more complex design problems. Students will broaden their skills and knowledge from previous coursework to develop a site and user-specific design project, at a mid-size building scale. A series of exercises will approach issues of context, program, scale, organization, space, form, structure and environmental systems. Design intentions will be investigated and tested at the scale of the detail with drawings and models. Prerequisite(s): ARSC 5005 and ARSC 5000

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 5110
courses.course_overview_raw: Contemporary Architecture: Theory and Practice in a Changing World. The purpose of this course is to investigate key concepts driving architecture and built form around the world, through an examination of the design and implementation process from concept to detail. Students will work individually and in teams to identify design drivers, program organization, conventions and innovation in architectural problem-solving. The course also considers the social roles and responsibilities of architects as public figures shaping the physical environments of communities, designing ‘places’ for people. Prerequisite(s): ARSC 5110

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 5350
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this course is to apply building science knowledge and skills to propose a high-performance sustainable project for Design Studio 4: Comprehensive. Through a series of lectures and assignments, students will execute holistic climate and site analysis, develop design strategies for building resilience, and set performance goals and drivers for the comprehensive project. A laboratory approach is used, developing iterations to improve process and results while promoting whole-building systems thinking. Prerequisite(s): ARSC 5350

courses.prerequisite_raw: BCIT ENGL 1177, or 6 credits BCIT Communication at 1100-level or above, or 3 credits of a university/college first-year social science or humanities course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Fosters abilities and values required for ethical decision making at work. Develops skills in logical analysis, a working knowledge of moral principles and theories, and the ability to diagnose and resolve moral disagreements commonly found at work. Examines and applies moral principles to historically famous cases in manufacturing, human resources, management, engineering, health care, and computing. Prerequisite(s): BCIT ENGL 1177, or 6 credits BCIT Communication at 1100-level or above, or 3 credits of a university/college first-year social science or humanities course.

curriculum_components.name: Level 7 (15 weeks)
curriculum_components.raw_text: Level 7 (15 weeks) Liberal Studies Electives: All students will be required to achieve an additional 6.0 credits of Liberal Studies electives in accordance with the BCIT policy on Liberal Studies course requirements . As part of the program, 3.0 of these credits will be offered in Level 7. Program head approval is required.

courses.prerequisite_raw: 60% in ARSC 6005
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course explores tectonics in architecture, relating form to materials, construction and structure. It is the study of architecture as a spatial concept expressed through the relative order of structure, detail and environmental context. The course investigates and tests the design with a built form, further refining the evolution of detail based on aesthetics, function, durability and current construction practice.​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in ARSC 6005

courses.prerequisite_raw: 60% in ARSC 6005
courses.course_overview_raw: ​The purpose of this studio is to introduce integrated design to the architectural process, applied to a large architectural project with complex systems requirements. A series of exercises will approach the synthesis of architectural principles with engineering concepts to propose architecturally integrated structures and environmental systems with advanced performance benchmarks. Students will be working independently, in teams and with industry consultants to achieve climate-resilient and regenerative designs. ​​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in ARSC 6005

courses.prerequisite_raw: 60% in ARSC 6005 and 50% in LIBS 7001
courses.course_overview_raw: ​The purpose of this course is to provide a structured approach to predesign research, analysis and response, in order to propose an informed Comprehensive project. A series of lectures, workshops and processes simulate professional practice for complex building pre-design. Working independently, in teams, with industry consultants and stakeholders, students will navigate regulatory frameworks to articulate site, program, budget and development parameters for the future Comprehensive project. The outcome of the course is an architectural pre-design brief ready for implementation in the project context (including authorities having jurisdiction, sociocultural issues, climate resilience, local design guidelines and urban design initiatives).​ Prerequisite(s): 60% in ARSC 6005 and 50% in LIBS 7001

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 6350
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this course is to apply building science knowledge and skills to the architectural design process. This course will integrate with ARSC 7006 (Predesign Studio). Through a series of lectures and work assignments, students will create a holistic site analysis. Design strategies will be integrated for resilience to set performance goals and drivers for the graduating project. Prerequisite(s): ARSC 6350

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The course provides an overview of the basic skills of a manager and applies these skills through a series of projects and case studies. It examines the evolution of management and the organizational culture and environment. It also teaches the decision-making skills and the skills involved in planning, organizing, leading and controlling, including planning and facilitating change, teamwork, applying motivational techniques and effective communication. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

curriculum_components.name: Level 8 (15 weeks)
curriculum_components.raw_text: Level 8 (15 weeks) Liberal Studies Electives: All students will be required to achieve an additional 6.0 credits of Liberal Studies electives in accordance with the BCIT policy on Liberal Studies course requirements . As part of the program, 3.0 of these credits will be offered in Level 8. Program head approval is required.

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 7005 and ARSC 7006 and ARSC 7350 ARSC 8355 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: ​The purpose of this studio is to execute comprehensive design for a large mixed-use high-performance building. Based on their pre-design brief, students will work through a series of exercises to develop industry-standard deliverables. The course models professional integrated design practices, including engagement with industry consultants and stakeholders. Students will demonstrate the ability to synthesize and apply knowledge and skills developed throughout their studies, applying leading-edge tools and techniques for high-performance building to a holistically sustainable architectural design, resolved from concept through to construction details.​ Prerequisite(s): ARSC 7005 and ARSC 7006 and ARSC 7350 ARSC 8355 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​The purpose of this course is to introduce the working processes and considerations of architectural practice. Students will gain familiarity with the different types of architectural practice organization and basic principles of project management, covering various roles and responsibilities. Case studies are used to illustrate stakeholder dynamics, project sociologistic, political and economics through real-world examples. Students will engage with building industry professionals and professional resources throughout the course.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: ARSC 7350 and ARSC 7006 ARSC 8005 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course holistically integrates previously learned tools and processes to inform and refine the graduating project. Through a series of lectures and studio assignments, students will pursue transformative architectural solutions based on course-specific performance goals. Students will self-evaluate building performance on an ongoing basis throughout the course.​ Prerequisite(s): ARSC 7350 and ARSC 7006 ARSC 8005 ‡ ( ‡ must be taken concurrently)

curriculum_components.name: Professional Electives (6.0 credits)
curriculum_components.raw_text: Professional Electives (6.0 credits): All students are required to complete 6.0 credits of Professional Electives. Please note: ARSC 7040 is available by approval of the program head. Contact the program head for additional elective options and for approval. Total Credits: 85.5

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Directed Studies enables the students to propose an area of study that would lend itself to increased learning through the exploration of study in Selected Topics areas. This Technical Elective course of study may vary from term to term and may include subjects such as: technology and design; environmental ethics; Studies abroad, architectural workshops; Evaluation, Communication and Monitoring of Project deliveries. The student must submit a Statement of Intent which is to be reviewed and approved by the Program Head prior to the student's ability to register for this elective. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The purpose of this course is to introduce traditional wood design and contemporary applications in large-scale, non-traditional buildings. Students will examine new engineered wood products, manufacturing technologies, and changes to building codes / other legislation to assess new possibilities for wood design and construction. This course will: i) provide an introduction to the attributes of wood as a building material; ii) give an overview of emerging technologies in frame, mass timber and composite construction in British Columbia; iii) explain how building industry use of wood fits within the broader context of environmental, economic and social sustainability; and iv) discuss the physical and psychological benefits of wood in architectural applications. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: October 1st* to May 31st* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Entrance requirements Competitive entry: Two-step process Preference will be given to applicants with: Requirements completed within the last five years A BCIT Diploma in Architectural and Building Technology Academic grades above 70% average Related experience Additional post-secondary academic courses Applicants with preferred entrance requirements are to submit transcripts and supporting documents with their online application. Applicants currently in the final term of the diploma program must be on track to graduate by July prior to the start of the intake and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion of their diploma. Step 1: Meet the entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Post-secondary: one of the following: A BCIT Diploma in Architectural and Building Technology or An equivalent diploma from a recognized institution with a minimum of 60.0 credits in architectural technology or related coursework BCIT will assess architectural technology, building technology or other engineering technology diplomas from other institutions for equivalency on an individual basis. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Complete the following form(s) for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for this program. Course by Course Self-Assessment Form [PDF] Complete this form only if you completed your diploma at an institution other than BCIT . Submit your portfolio: Submit a portfolio that includes examples of varied work. Pieces are to be student projects from former education or industry-related work and should demonstrate a cross section of skills. Examples of design-related work such as photography, fashion, art work, sculpture, graphics, painting, etc. that demonstrate highly-developed design skills can be included in the portfolio. Presentation of work: The portfolio is to be a maximum of 20 pages. The portfolio may not be larger than 8.5” x 11”. Reduce your work to fit this format. Present your portfolio in a clear, neat, professional manner. Label each page and include a note for each piece to explain why you have included it. Student projects or industry-related work must include details of the work you completed. When necessary, credit must be given to team members in a project. Submitting your portfolio: Please submit your portfolio digitally with your online application. Submissions must be a single PDF file. Do not use any links in your PDF portfolio. Compress your PDF file to the appropriate file size. If your file is too large, you can use ArtStation.com to host your portfolio. Please include the link to your ArtStation.com portfolio in an additional PDF and upload it with your online application. Name your PDF using this format: ARSC_INTAKEYEAR_A0NUMBER_PORTFOLIO.pdf. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment All applications will be reviewed by the program area at the application deadline. Department assessment is based on academic standing and portfolio evaluation. Admission is competitive and will be offered to the most qualified applicants. Portfolios will be assessed according to the following criteria: Quality of prior student or industry project work included in the portfolio. Quality, clarity, and completeness of the material included. Design of the portfolio- size, paper/image quality/typography, composition. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for re-admission may still be submitted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
